## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [7. März 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.103
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.103
- Datum: 7.3.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 7 Scans

pages.transcription:
Taft Hotel
Newhaven, Conn.                                          March 7th, 41

Dear Hanna & Manfred, Finally, after 4 weeks without news (except
that cable last week) your letter N° 4, Hanna, of Febr. 16th. Letter N° 3
has not yet arrived, but I hope we will still get it. There has
been such a muddle with the clippers lately, which were delayed,
damaged, flown another route, all owing to storms, that I am not
surprised about a mix-up in mail, bad as it is for us who wait
just as impatiently for your letters as you for ours and Eva's.
First of all, congratulations to Manfred for his exam! Actually we had
expected a telegram about it as it is after all a superior degree
and as far as I know, rather difficult. We hope that you follow
our advise and take Manfred to Bath for a good long rest after
this strain, Hanna. Why should he spend spring in London if he can
take his holiday in the country? I fully understand that you miss
Eva and that you sometimes wish she were still with you. It is an
unreasonable mood, yet I often feel the same about our being
here and think that in spite of all and everything I would prefer
to be in Rosemount with you and in our old surroundings. But
as you say yourself those are moods and one can reason them
away. - Now about Eva. At last I feel sure that you get regular
news as Sunday is writing-day whatever happens, and I asked
Mrs. Sch to add a few words to you now and then. I am in
constant touch, phoned Eva several times, and we had letters
- those sunday letters - from her and Mrs. Sch. She seems very
happy there, has come to like the new school - I wrote you
that she is after all in the Public School, a big modern
school and that we are not at all sorry that the Private
school was not possible in the end - has a piano teacher,
"a very ambitious one" - she writes, plays two Mozart sonatas, one
for practice and one for reading, has spent a weekend with
Salmon's, has been to a concert and feels altogether fine.
There are more children about her age now at Sch's, and
so far as I saw the children, I liked them very much.
Just when I was there last time, two Alstein-children, a boy
and a girl of 12 and 14 (third generation of the publishing firm)
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf Taft Hotel Briefpapier. Seite 1.

pages.transcription:
2)
just arrived, both extremely nice. One thing Eva is not too keen
about yet, is being outdoors, and as it was a nasty cold winter
I do not blame her for it. She is well equipped for it though,
for I bought her, what all the others wear there a snow suit, jacket
and trousers, wind- and waterproof, with a hood, and high snow boots.
Besides this she did not need anything to keep her warm as the
house and school are well-heated. (Not to have central-heating
and a huge refrigerator means extreme poverty in USA). Eva has holi-
days in the beginning of March and April and I think we will
take her here although it will not be very exciting for her, but we
would like to have her with us. On the whole I am very glad that
we have finally settled her with Mrs. Sch. and I feel that it
is the right thing for her. In all the deliberations and consi-
derations what would be best for Eva I have tried to do always
as I think you would have acted, and I feel quite sure that
you would have come to the same conclusions as I did and
chose Mrs. Sch. as a home with the advantage that there are
more children, more supervision and entertainment and a woman
which you would like very much, as the head of the whole who
spends all her time on it and runs it as much as possible on
family lines. As to schools, the one in Groton is good and you
would find the same story everywhere, all the English children
I hear about are about a year ahead of the American children. -
Now about us: we lead a quiet life with plenty of work and books,
enjoy the neighborhood of the library and are not at all lonely.
I have been in Newyork once and Stefan twice since we are here,
and we have had several visitors; one of them was Landshof who
told us that he had seen Manfred just before leaving and who
brought for Eva a little parcel which I hope he has sent her in
the meantime. He had the same idea like I with the Smollett
children, he said he would pass at Eva's place one day, and I
had to explain that it was 40 minutes by train. - I am glad
to hear that in Bath all is going well and that instead of Love
(where has she gone to?) you have another member of the Miller
family. I don't know how well Hilda cooks and I hope she likes
work better than her sister, but in any case it is good that you
have people on whom you can rely that they will not leave you.

3)
It is strange to think that there are people living now even in
the garden house and I imagine it pretty drafty now, although it
must be lovely in summer time. You were right in taking more
civil servants in the house; it will give you more work and no
profit, but on the other hand it is better to have them than
friends, and in this way you have more privacy to yourself.
Has Lizzy left Bath for good? Give Mr. Rauman once more
my thanks for advising you if business matters come up, I
wrote them a few weeks ago. I hope we will still get your last
letter in which it seems you wrote about business matters.
And please, give us occasionally when you have time, a list
of all that has happened with respect to Stefan's works and
publishers, who has paid royalties etc. etc. - just that we have an
idea what is going on. - About Hans: I quite agree with
what you say and I certainly did not mean to offer
him a rent. I must think the letter over carefully and
shall send it in a few days, and you will get a copy.
In the meantime don't give him anything. I am sorry
you have all this bother and wish he were not in London.
Mother has asked me now to get him an affidavit to USA.
But how can you guarantee such a man? With your brother
things are different and I was able to ask a stranger for it
with the best conscience. I do hope Mr. Landan's affidavit
is accepted as valid, it seems that he has given quite a
number already. - Now I have written a lot and made up
for the fact that last week I did not write, waiting from
day to day for a letter from you.
Kindest regards to all and best love
and kisses to you
Lotte

[Randnotiz links:] directly and next weeks I have to worry you about my book leaving for the accounts
as I have no files here and cannot reconstruct what I received before and after my
departure. I write you in detail that you may inform my accountant. We have no idea
whatever except what we will stay here few weeks

[Randnotiz unten:] Did you get Eva's address correctly?
Amity Hall
Mt. Airy Road
Croton-on-Hudson, N.Y.

Congratulations to Manfred and love to you all. Lotte has behaved very badly last
week, she had asthma-attacks in best Vienna style, now she is up again. The change
was perhaps too sudden from tropical climate to the icy winter and here in the old-
fashioned hotel the rooms are always like Turkish baths. I wrote today to Fredenthal
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief, Seite 3. Enthält Randnotizen und einen Nachsatz von Stefan Zweig.
